chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would detain a man if he evaded his creditors, then he would order his wealth to be divided among them in shares. If he refused, he would sell him and divide his wealth among them, meaning his wealth.
ai.seo_question: How does Islamic law handle a debtor who evades paying his creditors?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the judicial mechanism for debt recovery, highlighting the Imam’s authority to detain a debtor who evades creditors and subsequently liquidate his assets through proportional distribution. It underscores the practical application of *al-qismah* (division of property) in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring creditors receive their due shares even against the debtor's will. This procedure reflects the broader Islamic legal principle of preserving financial rights (*huquq al-nas*) through enforced compliance.
